Cardamom buns (kardemummabullar)

Swedish fika classic. Lots of cardamom in the dough, the filling and on top. Makes 24-30 buns.

Home page

Ingredients

Dough

  • 250mL milk
  • 25g fresh yeast (or 7g dry yeast)
  • 60g sugar
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1 tbsp freshly ground cardamom
  • 400g strong white flour
  • 75g butter, at room temperature

Filling

  • 100g butter, really soft
  • 80g sugar (2dL)
  • 1.5 tbsp freshly ground cardamom

Topping

  • 1 egg
  • 45g raw cane sugar (0.5dL)
  • 1 tbsp freshly ground cardamom

Recipe

Dough

  1. Warm the milk to 37C.
  2. Crumble the yeast in a large bowl. Pour the milk over and stir until dissolved.
  3. Add the sugar, salt, cardamom, almost all the flour and the butter in pieces.
  4. Knead 10 minutes with a stand mixer or 20 minutes by hand. The dough is ready when it pulls away from the bowl and you can touch it without it sticking to your fingers.
  5. Cover with a towel and let rise 30 minutes.
  6. Mix the filling. The butter really needs to be soft, otherwise it will spread well on the dough.

Shaping

  1. Turn the dough onto a floured surface, knead lightly and roll out to about 30x40cm. The dough can be sticky and not easy to work with: use more flour than usual on the bench, the dough and the rolling pin.
  2. Spread the filling over the whole surface.
  3. Fold the dough in half over the filling, roll lightly to even it out, cut 2cm strips. Stretch a strip slightly, twist it on the bench like a candy cane, coil into a spiral, tuck the end underneath.
  4. Place on baking sheets lined with parchment paper.
  5. Cover and let rise another 30 minutes.

Baking

  1. Preheat oven to 225C well ahead so it is really hot.
  2. Brush with beaten egg. Sprinkle with the raw sugar and cardamom mixed together. Putting it on before baking makes it stick and go slightly crunchy. Alternative: bake plain, brush with sugar syrup and sprinkle after.
  3. Bake in the middle of the oven 7-9 minutes.
  4. Cool on a wire rack.

Notes

Grind the cardamom seeds yourself in a mortar, rather than pre-ground: the taste and smell are night and day. Fresh yeast for sweet doughs and strong flour give fluffier buns. Room temperature butter and lukewarm milk. The filling quantities are 30% more than the original recipe.
